+# Pull-request staging environment for a RAILS app (FRAMEWORK=rails).
+# Copied into the app repo as .github/workflows/staging.yml by the bootstrap.
+#
+# Opening a PR against main stands a complete second copy of the app up on the
+# SAME droplet, serving on <app>-stg.<zone>; closing the PR destroys it. Pushing
+# to an open PR redeploys it. Jobs: test (gate) -> build+push -> deploy, and a
+# separate destroy job on `closed`.
+#
+# The Rails path is SQLite-only, so this workflow has no Postgres branch. The
+# environment's isolation from production comes from three things:
+#
+#   * its own compose project (<slug>-stg) — its own containers and its own
+#     app_data volume, so its database is a different file on a different volume
+#   * litestream.staging.yml, which replicates into that volume instead of Spaces
+#   * compose.override.yaml, which switches off the archive-to-Spaces loop
+#
+# Between them the environment holds no Spaces credentials at all, and cannot
+# write into the prefixes production restores from.
+#
+# ONE ENVIRONMENT PER APP, not one per PR: there is a single staging name, so
+# there is a single slot. The most recent PR to deploy holds it, recorded in
+# .staging-owner on the droplet. A second PR takes the slot over — destroying the
+# first PR's environment as it does — and closing a PR only tears the
+# environment down if that PR still owns it.
+#
+# Required repo config (seeded by bootstrap):
+#   var    STAGING_DOMAIN             - <app>-stg.<zone>; ABSENT DISABLES THIS
+#                                       WORKFLOW ENTIRELY (every job is gated on
+#                                       it), which is how an app whose infra/
+#                                       predates staging stays untouched
+#   plus the same DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN / SSH_PRIVATE_KEY / DOCR_REGISTRY /
+#   FIREWALL_ID / DROPLET_HOST / APP_SLUG the production deploy uses
+#
+# There is NO staging secret to maintain: the environment's signing key is
+# derived from SECRET_KEY_BASE inside the deploy job (one-way, fixed label), so
+# it differs from production's without anyone setting a second secret per app or
+# per pull request.
+name: staging
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    branches: [main]
+    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, closed]
+
+# One staging operation at a time for the whole repo — deploys and teardowns
+# alike. The slot is a single directory on a single droplet, so two PRs racing
+# to claim it must be serialized rather than merged. Queue rather than cancel:
+# an interrupted teardown leaks an environment, and an interrupted deploy can
+# leave migrations half-applied.
+concurrency:
+  group: staging-${{ github.repository }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  # The deploy comments the environment's URL on the PR.
+  pull-requests: write
+
+env:
+  REGISTRY: registry.digitalocean.com
+  # The PR number is the staging slot's owner, and part of every staging image
+  # tag — the teardown finds both by it.
+  PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
+
+jobs:
+  # Red tests block the staging deploy exactly as they block production's.
+  test:
+    # Three gates, all of them load-bearing:
+    #   * `closed` runs the destroy job instead
+    #   * no STAGING_DOMAIN means this app has no staging environment wired
+    #   * a PR from a FORK gets no secrets from GitHub, and must not: this
+    #     workflow holds the droplet's SSH key and the DO API token, and would
+    #     hand both to code nobody has reviewed. Such PRs are skipped, not failed.
+    if: >-
+      github.event.action != 'closed'
+      && vars.STAGING_DOMAIN != ''
+      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    env:
+      RAILS_ENV: test
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      # `ruby-version: .ruby-version`, not `ruby-version-file:` — see the note in
+      # deploy.ruby.yml: the file input is rejected by older resolutions of @v1.
+      - uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
+        with:
+          ruby-version: .ruby-version
+          bundler-cache: true
+
+      # Prepare the isolated test database before the Rails suite gates deployment.
+      - name: Run tests
+        run: |
+          bundle exec rails db:prepare
+          bundle exec rails test
+
+  build:
+    needs: test
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest # native amd64
+    outputs:
+      app_name: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.app_name }}
+      image: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.image }}
+      tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

+          if [ -z "$app_name" ]; then echo "::error::.app-name is empty or missing"; exit 1; fi
+          echo "app_name=$app_name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "image=${REGISTRY}/${{ vars.DOCR_REGISTRY }}/${app_name}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          # Staging images share the app's registry repository (the free tier
+          # allows exactly one) and are told apart by tag. The tag names the PR
+          # AND pins the commit: the PR part is what the teardown deletes, the
+          # SHA part is what keeps the deploy immutable. It is the PR's HEAD sha
+          # rather than github.sha, which for a pull_request event is the
+          # ephemeral merge commit and means nothing once the PR closes.
+          echo "tag=pr-${PR}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

+      - name: Install doctl
+        uses: digitalocean/action-doctl@v2
+        with:
+          token: ${{ secrets.DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Log in to DO Container Registry
+        run: doctl registry login --expiry-seconds 1200
+
+      - name: Set up Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
+
+      # No :latest here — that tag is production's, and a staging build must
+      # never become what an unpinned pull resolves to.
+      - name: Build and push image
+        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7

+# Runtime stack on the droplet for a RAILS app (FRAMEWORK=rails, which
+# always implies the SQLite backend). Copied to the app repo as
+# deploy/compose.yaml by the bootstrap. It mirrors compose.sqlite.yaml (the
+# Phoenix+SQLite stack) — same Litestream sidecar + restore, same blue/green
+# swap, same shared-Caddy routing — but boots a Rack/Puma app instead of an OTP
+# release:
+#
+#   * The app service runs `puma` (image CMD), not `bin/<app> start`. There is
+#     no PHX_SERVER gate and no APP_NAME — a Rack app serves unconditionally on
+#     $PORT.
+#   * Migrations run `rails db:prepare` (Active Record) in the one-off migrate
+#     runner, not `bin/<app> eval '<Module>.Release.migrate()'`.
+#   * The DB is a SQLite file on a NAMED DOCKER VOLUME (app_data -> /data),
+#     shared by both colors + the migrate runner. Litestream streams its WAL to
+#     Spaces continuously and restores it on a recreated droplet.
+#
+# Interpolated values (${...}) come from .env, written over SSH at deploy time:
+#   IMAGE            full image ref incl tag, e.g. registry.../app:<sha> (SHA-pinned)
+#   DOMAIN           public FQDN (matches the DNSimple A record / cert)
+#   APP_SLUG         this app's slug — names the compose project + network aliases
+#   DATABASE_PATH    on-volume path to the SQLite file, e.g. /data/app.db
+#   SECRET_KEY_BASE  Rack session secret (Rails `set :sessions`)
+#   LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID / LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   Spaces keypair
+#   BACKUP_BUCKET / BACKUP_ENDPOINT / BACKUP_REGION / BACKUP_PATH   replica target
+#
+# No secrets live in this file — only references. (locked decision 12)
+#
+# There is no proxy here: TLS and routing belong to the droplet's SHARED Caddy
+# (deploy/edge-compose.yaml, installed at /root/caddy), because one droplet can
+# host several apps and only one process can own :443. This stack joins the
+# shared `edge` network and publishes per-color aliases Caddy dials by name.
+
+# Every app on the droplet gets its own compose project, so its containers and
+# volumes (<slug>_app_data) can't collide with a neighbour's.
+name: ${APP_SLUG}
+
+# Shared definition for both colors (and the one-off migrate runner).
+x-app: &app
+  image: ${IMAGE}
+  restart: unless-stopped
+  env_file:
+    - .env
+  environment:
+    RAILS_ENV: "production"
+    RACK_ENV: "production"
+    # URL host for generated links; Rails reads APP_HOST where it builds URLs.
+    APP_HOST: ${DOMAIN}
+    PORT: "4000"
+    # SQLite file path (config/database.rb reads DATABASE_PATH).
+    DATABASE_PATH: ${DATABASE_PATH}
+  volumes:
+    # The SQLite file lives here, shared with the migrate runner + Litestream.
+    - app_data:/data
+  depends_on:
+    # Restore + permission fix must finish before the app opens the DB...
+    db_init:
+      condition: service_completed_successfully
+    # ...and the replicator must be running so writes are streamed off-box.
+    litestream:
+      condition: service_started
+  expose:
+    # Internal only — never published to the host. Caddy reaches it by name.
+    - "4000"
+  networks:
+    - web
+  healthcheck:
+    # Alive = the endpoint answers HTTP at all (HTTP 200 from /health).
+    # bash + /dev/tcp because the slim runtime image has no curl/wget.
+    test: ["CMD", "bash", "-c", "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/4000 && printf 'GET /health HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n' >&3 && grep -q '^HTTP/1.[01] 200 ' <&3"]
+    interval: 5s
+    timeout: 3s
+    retries: 12
+    start_period: 10s
+
+# Shared Litestream config: both the restore and replicate services read the
+# same /etc/litestream.yml (env-expanded against .env).
+x-litestream: &litestream
+  image: litestream/litestream:0.3.14
+  env_file:
+    - .env
+  volumes:
+    - app_data:/data
+    - ./litestream.yml:/etc/litestream.yml:ro
+  networks:
+    - web
+
+services:
+  # One-shot, runs as root before anything opens the DB. Two jobs:
+  #   1. Restore the SQLite file from Spaces IFF /data has no DB yet and a replica
+  #      exists (first-ever deploy: both false -> no-op; recreated droplet: empty
+  #      volume + existing replica -> full restore).
+  #   2. chown /data to the app's runtime uid (Debian 'nobody' = 65534) so the
+  #      app, which runs unprivileged, can create the DB + its -wal/-shm files.
+  # $$DATABASE_PATH is escaped so the container shell (not compose) expands it.
+  db_init:
+    <<: *litestream
+    restart: "no"
+    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
+    command:
+      - litestream restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists "$$DATABASE_PATH" && chown -R 65534:65534 /data
+
+  # Long-running: continuously replicate the WAL to Spaces. Runs as root (it can
+  # still read the nobody-owned DB and write its own shadow files under /data).
+  litestream:
+    <<: *litestream
+    restart: unless-stopped
+    command: ["replicate"]
+    depends_on:
+      db_init:
+        condition: service_completed_successfully
+
+  # The two colors are the only services on the shared `edge` network, and each
+  # carries a slug-qualified alias there — that name is what the droplet's Caddy
+  # dials (see deploy/site.caddy.tmpl). The alias must be unique ACROSS apps:
+  # every app on the host shares this network, so a bare `app_blue` would be
+  # ambiguous and Caddy would round-robin into someone else's app.
+  #
+  # `networks` is re-declared rather than inherited because the alias differs per
+  # color; a YAML merge key can't vary a value between the two.
+  app_blue:
+    <<: *app
+    networks:
+      web: {}
+      edge:
+        aliases:
+          - ${APP_SLUG}-blue
+
+  app_green:
+    <<: *app
+    networks:
+      web: {}
+      edge:
+        aliases:
+          - ${APP_SLUG}-green
+
+  # One-off migration runner (profile keeps it out of `up -d`):
+  #   docker compose run --rm migrate bundle exec rails db:prepare
+  # Never serves traffic, so it stays off `edge`.
+  migrate:
+    <<: *app
+    restart: "no"
+    profiles: ["tools"]
+
+volumes:
+  app_data:
+
+networks:
+  # Private to this app: the sidecars talk to nothing outside the project.
+  web:
+  # The droplet-wide network the shared Caddy is on. Created by edge.sh, external
+  # because it outlives any single app — tearing this stack down must not
+  # disconnect the other apps on the host.
+  edge:
+    external: true

+# name-agnostic command (`puma`), not a named OTP release. SQLite is the only
+# supported backend for the Rails path — the runtime carries libsqlite3 and
+# the DB file lives on a droplet volume (Litestream replicates it; see
+# deploy/compose.yaml).

+# file; RUBY_VERSION is an explicit override.

+ARG RUNNER_IMAGE="ruby:${RUBY_VERSION}-slim-bookworm"
+

+FROM ${BUILDER_IMAGE} AS builder
+
+# build-essential + the sqlite3 headers compile the sqlite3 native gem.
+RUN apt-get update -y \
+  && apt-get install -y build-essential git pkg-config libsqlite3-dev \
+  && apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

+# No BUNDLE_DEPLOYMENT: the scaffold ships no Gemfile.lock (it can't be generated
+# without the target Ruby), so bundler resolves from the Gemfile here and the
+# resulting image is the immutable, SHA-pinned artifact.

+    BUNDLE_WITHOUT="development:test" \

+    fi

+FROM ${RUNNER_IMAGE}
+

+# bash: the compose healthcheck uses a /dev/tcp probe (no curl in slim).

+    RACK_ENV="production" \
+    BUNDLE_PATH="/usr/local/bundle" \
+    BUNDLE_WITHOUT="development:test" \

+# Litestream db_init sidecar applies to the shared /data volume, so the app

+# name; the healthcheck hits 127.0.0.1:4000.
+CMD ["bundle", "exec", "puma", "-C", "config/puma.rb"]
